name: manual.release_candidate_roaming_mcw
description: Manual Windows release-candidate free-play handoff: daytime McWilliams/Basecamp start with bandits south, cannibals east, a zombie rider north, and a flesh raptor west. Every threat starts outside the initial reality bubble; the harness prepares and launches the audited save but sends no gameplay input after load.

manual_playtest.question: During ordinary roaming, do C-AOL's new hostile systems feel distinct, readable, and fair without announcing themselves like scripted test actors?
tester_notes: Play normally from the loaded daytime state; there is no required order or target checklist.
If you want orientation only: rider north, flesh raptor west, cannibals east, bandits south.
Save after a memorable encounter or failure so the resulting state can be audited with the note.
metadata_to_check_after: debug.log actor-specific live-plan and hostile-world rows
saved hostile-world sites, overmap entities, NPC positions, and monster state
the exact location/time immediately before a surprising interaction

evidence_contract.claim: manual load starts from a current staged roaming footing with all four requested hostile families nearby but outside immediate combat range
evidence_contract.load_only_verdict: manual handoff footing only; gameplay feel comes from Josef's unscripted play after handoff
